scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7058: I'm on PC4 in Location A and I cannot get to Laptop0
any more -- that's the machine the other group uses, one floor up but still
here in Location A. Everyone on my own floor is reachable fine; it is only
the upstairs machines I cannot reach. This worked before, so whatever joins
the floors has broken on your side. I won't pretend to know how the floors
are connected together -- that is your department, not mine. Check it and
fix whatever is wrong today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 routes between VLAN 10 (eth0.10,
  172.16.10.1) and VLAN 20 (eth0.20, 172.16.20.1) on its router-on-a-stick
  sub-interfaces, and mswitch1 trunks both VLANs. PC4 (172.16.10.x) reaches
  Laptop0 (172.16.20.x) with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a sub-interface / trunk fault that is not
  present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 10 cannot reach
VLAN 20 within Location A -- is NOT reproducible: router0's eth0.10 (172.16.10.1)
and eth0.20 (172.16.20.1) sub-interfaces are up with correct dot1Q tags, mswitch1
trunks both VLANs, and PC4 (VLAN 10) reaches Laptop0 (VLAN 20) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the VLAN10->VLAN20
path, finds it working, checks router0's sub-interfaces and mswitch1's trunk, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a sub-interface misconfig or a trunk drop
to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — PC4 (172.16.10.4) being unable to reach Laptop0 (172.16.20.10) — does not correspond to any real network fault. The two endpoints are in different IP subnets (VLAN 10: 172.16.10.0/24 and VLAN 20: 172.16.20.0/24), and inter-VLAN routing between them is provided by router0 in a router-on-a-stick configuration. Router0 holds eth0.10 (172.16.10.1/24) and eth0.20 (172.16.20.1/24) as the respective gateways for the two floors, reachable via tagged VLAN subinterfaces through mswitch1 to switch1.

Direct testing confirms fully functional end-to-end connectivity: ping from PC4 to Laptop0 returns 0% packet loss in both directions, and a traceroute confirms the correct two-hop path (PC4 → router0 → Laptop0). Switch1's bridge configuration correctly places PC4's port (eth1) in br_vlan10 and Laptop0's port (eth7) in br_vlan20, and the FDB tables on both switch1 and mswitch1 show the correct MAC addresses learned on the correct ports for both hosts. There are no iptables or ip6tables rules on any transit device (router0, mswitch1, switch1) — all chains are ACCEPT with zero entries.

The root cause of the ticket is a false premise: the network is healthy and the connectivity the user believes is broken is actually working correctly. No corrective action is required; the engineering team should advise the user to retest and clarify what specific operation they observed failing, as it is not reproducible at the IP layer.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states router0 has eth0.10 and eth0.20 as tagged subinterfaces and describes mswitch1 carrying those VLANs (supported by FDB entries), satisfying the baseline healthy-note requirement.
